test_description: Compare OddAlerts' documented 'frozen pre-match stats' behavior (include_frozen=true) against a manually reconstructed leakage-safe pre-match rolling window, for a single real, verifiable fixture.

target_fixture.note: home_played:23 on the fixture object itself is OddAlerts' own statement that Arsenal had played exactly 23 prior league matches this season before this kickoff.

result.interpretation: 38 is the FULL 2024/25 season total (season had 38 played by result-completion time of this audit), not a snapshot frozen at matchday 24. This includes matches that happened AFTER the target fixture -- i.e. future information leaking into what is documented as a pre-match feature.

method_B_self_reconstructed_rolling_wind.call: GET /api/fixtures/between?teams=5303&seasons=6484&from=1723500000&to=1738454400&include=stats  (Arsenal, 2024/25 season, strictly before the 2025-02-02 kickoff)

result.matches_this_exactly: 23 -- matches the fixture object's own home_played:23 field exactly, confirming this is the correct pre-match sample.
result.note: All 23 matches had xg populated (all fell after the Feb-May 2024 xG cutover), so xG-based pre-match features are usable here specifically because this fixture is late enough in the 2024/25 season.

conclusion: Method A (OddAlerts' own include_frozen=true) is NOT leakage-safe as documented and should not be used for feature construction. Method B (pull raw fixtures via /fixtures/between filtered to teams+season+date-range strictly before kickoff, then aggregate ourselves) produces the exact correct sample size and is the recommended architecture. This is not a hypothetical recommendation -- it was verified end-to-end against a real match on real data in this test.
